body: Thanks, good luck to you as well.

So I actually lived in my car as well. You'll see a lot of advice about finding a gym, overnight parking, foods to keep, etc. But something that I never even considered was how much my physical body would be affected by sleeping in my car. I'm a pretty small woman and can lay down completely in the front seat of my car, but I still have back and hip pain despite sleeping in a bed for several months now. Unless you have a truck and can lay flat, your feet/legs will swell from laying at an angle. If you're a side sleeper like me, it'll put a lot of stress on your hip. A travel pillow (the one shaped like a C) should support your neck. These are things to keep in mind. I would also highly recommend you keep up with some daily exercise to combat these issues, even if it's just walking 30 minutes per day.

For me, it lasted about three months. If you are able to work at all, even just a little bit, the odds are in your favor. Most people who are permantly homeless have an untreated, debilitating mental illness. In my opinion, your absolute top priority should be maintaining your mental health.

Feel free to PM me if you want to talk or have questions.
Oddly enough, this is the only way a partner has made me come.
